---
title: "Install MISP 3.0 on Debian 13"
---

Use this guide to install MISP on a clean Debian 13 “Trixie” server, the current Debian stable series.
It uses the [Debian 13 installer on `3.0_wip`](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/blob/3.0_wip/INSTALL/INSTALL.debian13.sh) to set up Apache with PHP 8.4, MariaDB 11.8, Redis, and Supervisor.
Use the current Debian 13 point release with its security updates. [Debian stable release information](https://www.debian.org/releases/stable/)

::: {.callout-note}
`3.0_wip` is the MISP 3.0 development branch.
Evaluate the installer on a disposable host before deployment. It updates system packages and service configuration, initializes a new database, and creates credentials.
For an existing MISP 2.5 database, use the [offline upgrade procedure](../upgrade-2-5-to-3-0/index.qmd).
:::

## Prepare the host {#debian-install-prepare}

Start with an account with `sudo` and a clean host. The commands use `/var/www/MISP` and the `www-data` account.
Configure the DNS name that analysts and API clients will use, and provision the certificate chain and its private key for that name.
Keep access restricted to administrators during setup.
Size the host and database storage for the expected load. [Instance requirements](../requirements/index.qmd)

Install prerequisites for the installer and its dependency builds.
The Debian script checks the release with `lsb_release` and uses the `mysql` command supplied by `mariadb-client-compat` on Debian 13.

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install ca-certificates curl openssl gnupg lsb-release \
  mariadb-client-compat php-pear python3-dev make unzip procps iproute2
lsb_release -sr
```

The last command should report `13`. [Debian MariaDB compatibility package](https://packages.debian.org/trixie/mariadb-client-compat)

## Configure the installer {#debian-install-configure}

Download the installer from the current branch and review it in a text editor before running it.

```bash
curl --fail --location --output INSTALL.debian13.sh \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MISP/MISP/3.0_wip/INSTALL/INSTALL.debian13.sh
```

Set the following variables in the downloaded script for your host.
Use a certificate chain and key readable by the installer, and replace the hostname, paths, and GnuPG identity with your own values.

```bash
MISP_DOMAIN='misp.example.org'
MISP_BASEURL="https://${MISP_DOMAIN}"
PATH_TO_SSL_CERT='/etc/ssl/certs/misp-fullchain.pem'
PATH_TO_SSL_KEY='/etc/ssl/private/misp.key'
GPG_EMAIL_ADDRESS='misp@example.org'
```

The Debian installer assigns these variables inside the script. Edit those assignments directly.
The generated Apache virtual host serves HTTPS on port 443 and uses `app/webroot` as its document root.

### Check GnuPG and the scheduler {#debian-install-adjustments}

In the downloaded script's **Generating PGP key** section, check that the application user's GnuPG directory is created before key generation and that the batch command uses loopback pinentry.
If the script lacks those steps, replace its `gpg --quick-generate-key` invocation with the following.
The directory must already exist when GnuPG starts its agent on Debian 13.

```bash
sudo install -d -o "$APACHE_USER" -g "$APACHE_USER" -m 0700 \
  "$MISP_PATH/.gnupg"
error_check "GnuPG directory creation"
sudo -u "$APACHE_USER" gpg --homedir "$MISP_PATH/.gnupg" \
  --quick-generate-key --batch --pinentry-mode loopback \
  --passphrase "$GPG_PASSPHRASE" "$GPG_EMAIL_ADDRESS" ed25519 sign never \
  &>> "$logfile"
```

In the same script, check the two keys below in the generated Supervisor `[program:scheduler]` section.
Set them to these values if the section uses `start_worker scheduler` or specifies more than one process.
The dedicated `scheduler_worker` command dispatches scheduled work. [Scheduler implementation](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/blob/3.0_wip/app/Console/Command/SchedulerWorkerShell.php)

```ini
command=$MISP_PATH/app/Console/cake scheduler_worker
numprocs=1
```

## Install and verify MISP {#debian-install-check}

Run the configured script from a private terminal. The installer prints generated credentials during setup.

```bash
bash -n INSTALL.debian13.sh
sudo bash ./INSTALL.debian13.sh
```

The installer checks out `3.0_wip` and initializes its matching submodules.
It loads `INSTALL/MARIADB.sql`, applies the application updates, and sets up the `misp-workers` group.
Check the exit status and the installer log if a step fails.

Keep `/root/misp_settings.txt` and `/var/log/misp_install.log` private.
They can contain passwords and API credentials.
Restrict the Supervisor configuration file too, since it contains credentials for the local worker-management API.
Restore private permissions on the GnuPG home after the installer's final permissions pass.

```bash
sudo chmod 0600 /etc/supervisor/supervisord.conf
sudo chmod -R go-rwx /var/www/MISP/.gnupg
sudo apache2ctl configtest
sudo systemctl status apache2 mariadb redis-server supervisor --no-pager
sudo supervisorctl status 'misp-workers:*'
sudo -u www-data /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin schemaDiagnostics
sudo -u www-data /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin getWorkers
sudo -u www-data git -C /var/www/MISP status --short --branch
sudo ss -lntp
```

Confirm that schema diagnostics show `Pending: 0` and `Failed: 0`.
Check the worker queues and confirm that the scheduler has one running process.
Verify that MariaDB, Redis, and the Supervisor API are reachable only where required. For the single-host setup, use local connections for these services.
The installation was tested on Debian 13.8 in a container with services started directly. Use the `systemctl` check above on your Debian host.

Open the HTTPS URL from a trusted client, verify the certificate and redirects, then sign in as `admin@admin.test` with the generated password from `/root/misp_settings.txt`.
Replace the bootstrap credentials, check the local organization and distribution defaults, and save and search for an unpublished, organization-only test event.
Verify that a background job completes before enabling sync or scheduled feeds. [First steps after login](../quick-start/index.qmd#first-steps-after-login) · [Background worker checks](../administration/index.qmd#admin-background-jobs)

For an upgrade from 2.5, rehearse on a restored copy using your Debian database and PHP versions.
Use the latest `3.0_wip` checkout and the offline `Admin runUpgrade` flow in the [upgrade guide](../upgrade-2-5-to-3-0/index.qmd).
The `www-data` account and `apache2` restart steps apply to this Debian layout.
